sections.title: Basic Concept of Algebra
sections.content: In Algebra, we work with unknown numbers (like x, y) and mathematical operations involving them. Example: If x + 5 = 12, then x = 7.

sections.title: Simple Equations
sections.content: Solving equations means finding the value of the unknown. Example: 2x + 3 = 11 → 2x = 8 → x = 4

sections.title: Substitution
sections.content: If x = 3 is known, substitute it into an expression to find the value. Example: 2x + 5 → 2*3 + 5 = 11

sections.title: Polynomials
sections.content: A polynomial is a sum of terms with different powers of x. Example: x² + 5x + 6. These can be simplified by addition, subtraction, or factoring.

sections.title: Multiplication and Division Rules
sections.content: Use the distributive rule to simplify equations and polynomials. Example: x(x + 5) = x² + 5x

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Forgetting the negative sign
2) Not applying the same operation to both sides of the equation
3) Incorrect addition or subtraction of polynomial terms

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Algebra = Unknowns + Equations + Polynomials. Solve step by step using substitution and simplification.
